attempted_claim: Let S=A(E,tau) be the four-dimensional Sklyanin algebra over algebraically closed k of characteristic 0 with tau of exact order 5, hence PI of degree 5, let W in S_2 be its two-dimensional space of degree-two central elements, let Omega_sing in W be a named singular member of the Smith-Van den Bergh pencil of four singular quadrics, and let Q_sing=S/S Omega_sing. Prove or disprove that Q_sing is module-finite over the image of Z(S) with PI-degree 5 and that the Azumaya locus of Q_sing equals the smooth locus of its central spectrum. A complete answer gives the center of Q_sing, its PI-degree and rank over the center, equations for its singular locus, and either a proof of Azumaya-smooth coincidence or an explicit witness maximal ideal with smoothness, Azumaya membership, discriminant-vanishing certificates and the full list of simple Q_sing-module dimensions above it, distinguishing the singular-quadric case excluded from the Van den Bergh translation equivalence.
claim_type: PI-finiteness and Azumaya-equals-smooth for singular central quadric quotient
decisive_failure: No noncommutative computer-algebra system was available locally (python3 with sympy and numpy only), the controlled literature call failed on credentials, and the reference web fetch failed on transport, so the exact order-5 Sklyanin data, Smith-Tate center relations, singular normal form, and witness certificates could not be grounded to audit standard within the clock.
